titleStmt.title: No. 913
The Secretary of State to the United States Mission at the United Nations

div.head:
No. 913
The Secretary of State to the United States Mission at the United Nations
div.p: 241. We believe that continued debate in SC of Egyptian restrictions on Suez Canal traffic will only exacerbate situation NE without producing practical results. Israel appears intent on pressing issue in SC and Egypt on resisting pressures from SC.

To break stalemate we believe SC might adopt resolution referring question legality continuing Egyptian restrictions to ICJ thus forestalling further SC debate until opinion rendered on grounds matter sub judice. At same time SC could note Azmi October 14 statement that Egypt “has refrained from any interference with vessels conveying goods to Israel or coming from Israel ports and passing through Suez Canal”. Although probably not intended by Azmi to encompass Israel flag ships, policy enunciated if carried out would remove in practice large part of burden of restrictions on Israel. Formal note of policy by SC would tend to insure its implementation
and lessen deterrent effect restrictions emphasized by Eban.

Accordingly USUN requested comment on tentative draft resolution given below and discuss matter with UK delegation. We envisage that USUN would subsequently discuss idea with Egyptians in confidence and without showing them resolution. We hope Egypt will feel able concur in suggested procedure. Particularly useful would be statement by Egyptian delegate reaffirming declaration quoted above.
Noting its resolution S/2322 of September 1, 1951,
Noting that the Government of Egypt has not revoked decrees imposing certain restrictions upon the passage through the Suez Canal of ships and goods bound to or from Israel,

Noting the statement by the Representative of Egypt in the Security Council that the Government of Egypt “has refrained from any interference with vessels conveying goods to Israel or coming from Israel ports and passing through the Suez Canal,”
Considering that there are involved questions of a legal nature in connection with the determination of privileges of freedom of transit through the Suez Canal,
Considering further the desirability of an adequate consideration of these legal issues and a pronouncement thereon by the International Court of Justice,
Requests the International Court of Justice to give an advisory opinion on the following question:

Is the present legislation and practice of the Government of Egypt with respect to freedom of transit through the Suez Canal consistent with international obligations of the Government of Egypt, taking into account (a) the decisions and recommendation of the United Nations organs on the Palestine and Suez Canal transit questions, (b) the Suez Canal Convention of 1888, and (c) other relevant international agreements and rules of international law.”

We now informed Israel intends send additional Israel flag ships to Suez Canal as test cases. If Egypt accepts proposal suggested above, we could urge Israel refrain from further moves until ICJ opinion rendered on grounds new Egyptian policy noted by Security Council largely removes economic burden restrictions on Israel.

note.p: Repeated to Cairo, Tel Aviv, London, and Paris.
